newsitem.title: USA: Broin jury selection seen extending beyond July 4.
newsitem.headline: Broin jury selection seen extending beyond July 4.

text.p: The judge overseeing the secondhand-smoke trial against U.S. tobacco companies on Tuesday said jury selection would likely go on until after the three-day Fourth of July weekend.
Questioning of potential jurors in the landmark class-action lawsuit, filed on behalf of thousands of flight attendants, is now in its fourth week.
By late Tuesday morning, 87 people had passed initial screening, putting them in a pool of standbys from which six jurors and 10 alternates will be selected.
Dade County Circuit Court Judge Robert Kaye said in court that 125 standby jurors would be required, since each side can dismiss without explanation as many as 45 people.
"I'll shoot for 125 people in the pool," Kaye said. The jury-selection process would last until at least July 7, he said.
A telephone company worker, a retired electrical engineer and a house painter were among the people placed in the standby pool on Tuesday.

Testimony in the case, known as Norma Broin vs. Philip Morris Cos Inc et al. is expected to last two months or longer. Afterwards a jury will decide whether secondhand smoke on U.S. passenger flights caused sicknesses among thousands of flight attendants.
